concerns.text: FR-006: 'The system MUST measure and report the inference latency reduction factor... on a standard CPU (2 cores)' lacks a verifiable procedure. It does not specify the input document length, number of iterations for averaging, or warm-up steps required to produce a deterministic latency measurement. Without a fixed input profile (e.g., '32k token document, 10 runs, 2 warm-up'), the result is non-reproducible.

US-2 Acceptance Scenario 2: '...returns a valid cluster assignment within 50ms on a standard CPU (2 cores)' sets a quantitative threshold (50ms) without defining the input size (chunk ID lookup is O(1) but depends on index size) or the hardware environment (which CPU model?). This makes the acceptance criterion unverifiable as written.

US-3 Acceptance Scenario 1: Requires outputting 'latency reduction factor' but does not define the measurement protocol (e.g., 'average of 5 runs on a 32k token document'). The metric is undefined without a fixed input context and measurement method, making it impossible to verify if the system 'delivers' this value consistently.

SC-005: 'The memory footprint... is measured against the dynamic retrieval module's runtime memory usage' lacks a verifiable procedure. It does not specify how to isolate the 'dynamic retrieval module' memory usage from the rest of the model (e.g., embedding layers, KV cache) or the measurement tool (e.g., `psutil`, `tracemem`). Without a defined isolation method, the comparison is ambiguous.
